declarations.docstring: The underlying vector space of a binary biproduct is linearly equivalent to the product of its components.
The character of a binary biproduct is the sum of the two component characters.
A zero representation has the zero character at every group element.
A complete family of simple representations expresses every character with natural coefficients.
The coefficients arising from a complete simple family give the corresponding Hom-space dimension formula.
The dimension of maps from a fixed representation into a finite biproduct is the sum of the component dimensions.
For a complete pairwise distinct simple family, Hom-space dimensions are obtained from the associated multiplicities.
Maps between members of a pairwise nonisomorphic simple family have dimension one on the diagonal and zero otherwise.
Maps into a representation assembled from a finite family have dimension given by the weighted component sum.
Maps from a fixed representation to a finite biproduct are linearly equivalent to families of component maps.
A morphism of representations commutes with the action of each group element.
A representation associated with a finite family and a natural-number multiplicity for each member.
The multiplicity function assigned to a representation relative to a family of representations.
A complete pairwise distinct simple family reconstructs every representation from its assigned multiplicities.
